<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-options.mjs from the TSDoc in choropleth-kit 0.3.0. Do not edit by hand. -->

> Generated from `choropleth-kit` **0.3.0**.

These are the options you pass to `<ChoroplethMap>`. The same options are accepted by `<Choropleth.Root>` and `useChoropleth()`, except the ones marked **Preset only**: they configure pieces the preset renders for you (`legend`, `breadcrumb`, `markers`, `renderTooltip`, `ariaLabel`). With the compound API you configure those on the matching piece instead. See [Choosing an API level](/api-levels/).

`TDatum` is the type of one row of your `data`; it is inferred from it.

Some options exist only for certain `variant` values (`sequential`, `diverging`, `categorical`, `bubble`). They are labelled below. For the other types mentioned here, see the [React API](/reference/react/) and the [Core API](/reference/core/).


## Geography and data

### `geography`

`GeographyInput`

Optional

TopoJSON or GeoJSON, a promise, or `() => import("…")`. Already-loaded data must have a stable
reference (a module constant or `useMemo`).

### `geographyKey`

`string`

Optional

Cache key for an async geometry (otherwise the function's identity is used).

### `objectName`

`string`

Optional

Name of the TopoJSON object to draw (for example `"countries"`). Not needed with GeoJSON.

### `region`

`RegionProp`

Optional

Restricts the map to a continent, a subregion or some countries, from the first frame (no flight, no
world around it): `"europe"`, `"westernEurope"`, `"eu27"`, `"ES"`, `["ES", "PT"]`, `["europe", "MA"]`.
It matches `feature.id` (or `getFeatureId`) against ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Overseas territories
(Guiana, Svalbard, Hawaii…) are left out so they do not shrink the framing. Russia is in no preset:
ask for it with `"RU"`. With `drill` it restricts the root level; the levels below bring their own
geometry. Data outside the region is ignored without warnings (`joinReport.outOfRegion`).

### `filterFeatures`

`(feature: Feature) => boolean`

Optional

Discards regions before anything else (e.g. Antarctica: `(f) => f.id !== "010"`).

### `data`

`readonly TDatum[] | undefined | ((ctx: DrillContext) => readonly TDatum[] | undefined)`

**Required**

`undefined` = loading (the previous data is kept, no warnings); `[]` = loaded and empty. With `drill`
it can be a selector for the current level: `({ depth, parentId }) => rows.filter(…)`.

### `getId`

`(datum: TDatum) => string`

**Required**

Returns the region id a row belongs to. It is matched exactly against each region's id (`feature.id`, or what `getFeatureId` returns).

### `getFeatureId`

`(feature: Feature) => string | undefined`

Optional

The region's id if it is not `feature.id` (e.g. `(f) => f.properties?.iso_a2`).

### `loading`

`boolean`

Optional

Forces the data loading state (pulse) even if `data` is defined.

### `onGeographyError`

`(error: Error) => void`

Optional

Called if the async geometry load fails. Without this, a console warning is issued.

### `fallbackPoints`

`Readonly<Record<string, Point>>`

Optional

Microstates that do not exist in the geometry (Andorra, Monaco…): `{ AD: [1.52, 42.51] }`. A datum
whose id joins no region but is listed here is painted as a dot, with the datum's color. In
`bubble`, as a bubble.


## Variant and scale

### `variant`

**Required**

**`sequential`**: `"sequential"`

> What the map means: `"sequential"`, `"diverging"`, `"categorical"` or `"bubble"`. Each variant requires its own accessors.

**`diverging`**: `"diverging"`

> What the map means: `"sequential"`, `"diverging"`, `"categorical"` or `"bubble"`. Each variant requires its own accessors.

**`categorical`**: `"categorical"`

> What the map means: `"sequential"`, `"diverging"`, `"categorical"` or `"bubble"`. Each variant requires its own accessors.

**`bubble`**: `"bubble"`

> What the map means: `"sequential"`, `"diverging"`, `"categorical"` or `"bubble"`. Each variant requires its own accessors.

### `getValue`

**Required** · Only with `sequential`, `diverging`, `bubble`

**`sequential`, `diverging`**: `(datum: TDatum) => number | null`

> The number each row paints. Return `null` for no data (a `0` is data, not an absence).

**`bubble`**: `(datum: TDatum) => number | null`

> ABSOLUTE value that gives the circle's AREA. `null`s and values ≤ 0 draw no circle.

### `getCategory`

`(datum: TDatum) => string | null`

**Required** · Only with `categorical`

The category each row belongs to, matched against `categories`. Return `null` for no data.

### `getColorValue`

`(datum: TDatum) => number | null`

Optional · Only with `bubble`

Second metric → the bubble's color (bivariate, diverging scale).

### `getCoordinates`

`(datum: TDatum) => readonly [number, number] | null`

Optional · Only with `bubble`

The datum's [lon, lat]. Without this, the bubble goes at its region's centroid.

### `maxRadius`

`number`

Optional · Only with `bubble`

Radius in pixels of the largest bubble. Defaults to 24.

### `color`

`string`

Optional · Only with `bubble`

Single color when there is no `getColorValue`.

### `categories`

`readonly CategorySpec[]`

Optional · Only with `categorical`

Fixed order and colors.

### `palette`

Optional

**`sequential`**: `SequentialPaletteName | CustomRamp`

> A named ramp, or your own colors: `{ from: "#fff", to: "#2563eb" }` or `["#fff", "#888", "#2563eb"]`.

**`diverging`**: `DivergingPaletteName | DivergingRamp`

> A named ramp, or your own: `{ negative, neutral, positive }`.

**`categorical`**: `CategoricalPaletteName`

> A named categorical palette. Defaults to `tableau10`. Pass `categories` to set the colors yourself.

**`bubble`**: `DivergingPaletteName`

> Diverging palette for the bubble color when `getColorValue` is set. Defaults to `rdbu`.

### `classification`

`Classification`

Optional · Only with `sequential`, `diverging`, `bubble`

How values are grouped into classes: `{ method: "quantile" }`, `{ method: "quantize" }`, `{ method: "linear" }` (continuous) or `{ method: "threshold", thresholds: [...] }`. Defaults to 5 quantiles for `sequential` and 5 equal classes around `midpoint` for `diverging`. See [Classification and domain](/concepts/classification-and-domain/).

### `domain`

Optional · Only with `sequential`, `diverging`

**`sequential`**: `readonly [number, number]`

> Fixed `[min, max]` (a share: `[0, 100]`) instead of the data's range. Values outside it are clamped.

**`diverging`**: `readonly [number, number]`

> Fixed `[min, max]`, used as given (it need not be symmetric around the midpoint).

### `midpoint`

`number`

Optional · Only with `diverging`, `bubble`

The neutral value of the diverging scale. Defaults to `0`. Without `domain`, the range is symmetric around it.

### `formatValue`

`(value: number) => string`

Optional

Formats a number for the tooltip and the legend.

### `emptyFill`

`string`

Optional

Fill for regions without data. Defaults to a light gray, or the theme's empty color.

### `emptyLabel`

`string`

Optional

If given, the legend includes a "no data" item with this text.

### `emptyPattern`

`"none" | "hatch" | "dots"`

Optional

Pattern over regions without data (`"hatch"`, `"dots"`); it beats the theme's.


## Layout and appearance

### `theme`

`ThemeName | ChoroplethTheme`

Optional

`"light"` · `"dark"` · `"minimal"` · `"contrast"` or an object (`defineTheme`, `extendTheme`).

### `classNames`

`ChoroplethClassNames`

Optional

One class of yours per piece, ADDED to the `cm-*` one (Tailwind, CSS Modules).

### `className`

`string`

Optional

A class added to the root element.

### `style`

`CSSProperties`

Optional

Inline styles for the root element.

### `unstyled`

`boolean`

Optional

Removes all the base CSS. You then style every piece yourself; the `data-*` attributes still apply.

### `aspectRatio`

`number | "auto"`

Optional

Width / height of the map. `"auto"` derives it from the geometry's bounds (Chile comes out tall,
Norway wide). 960 / 500 by default, the world's proportion.

### `width`

`number`

Optional

Fixed size. If missing, the container (`containerRef`) is measured.

### `height`

`number`

Optional

Fixed height in pixels. Without it, the height comes from the container width and `aspectRatio`.

### `projection`

`ProjectionName`

Optional

The map projection, by name. Defaults to `equalEarth`, which keeps areas comparable.

### `legend`

`LegendOptions | false`

Optional · **Preset only**

`false` hides the legend.

### `breadcrumb`

`{ position?: LegendPosition; } | false`

Optional · **Preset only**

Drill breadcrumbs (only with `drill`). `false` hides them; top-left by default.

### `markers`

`readonly MarkerSpec[]`

Optional · **Preset only**

HTML pins or cards anchored to `[lon, lat]` that follow the map. Each one's `children` is its content.

### `regionLabels`

`boolean | RegionLabelsOptions<TDatum>`

Optional

Region names on the map (`true` for the defaults). Labels avoid overlapping: lower-priority ones are
hidden and zooming in reveals more. Not to be confused with `labels` (UI texts).

### `labels`

`Partial<ChoroplethLabels>`

Optional

UI texts (i18n). English by default; `es` is exported.

### `ariaLabel`

`string`

Optional · **Preset only**

Accessible name of the map (`aria-label` on the `<svg>`). Always set it.


## Interaction

### `selectedId`

`string | null`

Optional

Controlled: you are in charge. `null` = nothing selected. Without this, the library holds the state.

### `defaultSelectedId`

`string | null`

Optional

Uncontrolled: the initial selection.

### `onSelectedIdChange`

`(id: string | null) => void`

Optional

Called when the selection changes (click on a region; click on the selected one = `null`).

### `dimOthers`

`DimOthers`

Optional

Dims the rest of the map. Defaults to `"selection"`.

### `onItemClick`

`(item: MapItem<TDatum>) => void`

Optional

Click on a region or a point (`item.kind`).

### `onItemHover`

`(item: MapItem<TDatum> | null) => void`

Optional

Hover (or first tap, on touch). `null` on leaving. Only called when the item changes.

### `getRegionStyle`

`(region: Region<TDatum>) => RegionStyle | undefined`

Optional

Per-region style based on its data: `(r) => r.datum?.estimated ? { opacity: 0.6 } : undefined`. Priority:
`getRegionStyle` > scale color > `emptyFill`. Do not define `fill` on `.cm-region` in CSS: it would beat the datum.

### `renderTooltip`

`(context: TooltipContext<TDatum>) => ReactNode`

Optional · **Preset only**

Tooltip content. Without this: the region's name and formatted value.


## Camera

### `zoom`

`boolean | ZoomOptions`

Optional

Zoom and pan. On by default; `false` = static map. The wheel zooms with the mouse over
the map (`wheel: "always"`); for maps inside a long page use `wheel: "cooperative"`.

### `focusId`

`string | null`

Optional

Flies to this region (id) when it changes; with `null` it returns to the fit. On the **first render**
it does not fly: it places the camera directly. It is the declarative form of `zoomTo`.

### `focusBounds`

`Readonly<Record<string, LonLatBounds | null>>`

Optional

Explicit framings per region, in [[lonW, latS], [lonE, latN]]. They are merged with the library's
(`DEFAULT_FOCUS_BOUNDS`: Spain **with the Canary Islands**). `{ ES: null }` returns to the geometric
framing (main body) for that region.


## Drill-down

### `drill`

`readonly DrillLevel<TDatum>[] | DrillController<TDatum>`

Optional

Drill-down: the list of levels (uncontrolled) or a `useDrillDown` (controlled).
With `drill`, the geometry comes from the levels and `geography` is ignored.

### `onDrill`

`(event: DrillEvent<TDatum>) => void`

Optional

When a level change STARTS (the route is already updated).

### `onDrillEnd`

`(event: DrillEvent<TDatum>) => void`

Optional

When the new level has finished being shown.

### `onDrillError`

`(event: { error: unknown; ctx: DrillContext; }) => void`

Optional

If a level's geometry fails (or has 0 regions): it goes back to the previous level.

### `onDrillIntent`

`(ctx: DrillContext) => void`

Optional

The pointer has stayed 150 ms over a region you can drill into (or, on touch, it was tapped once):
`ctx` is that of the level it would go down to. Use it to preload data (`queryClient.prefetchQuery`);
that level's geometry is already preloaded by the map. Called once per dwell.


## Diagnostics

### `onJoinReport`

`(report: JoinReport) => void`

Optional

Called every time the data↔regions join result changes (also in production).

### `diagnostics`

`boolean`

Optional

Console warning about ids that did not join. Outside production only. Defaults to `true`.
